questions.explanation: Frugal means careful with money and avoiding waste, which is the same as thrifty.
questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to FRUGAL.

questions.explanation: Obscure means unclear or hard to understand, so its opposite is clear.
questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to OBSCURE.

questions.explanation: Since is used with a specific starting point in time, such as the year 2019.
questions.q: Fill in the blank: She has been working at this bank ___ 2019.

questions.explanation: With neither/nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, so the plural subject students needs were listening, not was listening.
questions.q: Identify the part with an error: Neither the teacher (A) nor the students (B) was listening (C) attentively. No error (D)

questions.explanation: To bite the dust means to suffer defeat or failure, as in losing a contest.
questions.q: What does the idiom TO BITE THE DUST mean?

questions.explanation: The correct preposition after good when referring to a skill or subject is at.
questions.q: Fill in the blank: He is very good ___ mathematics.

questions.explanation: Diligent means hardworking and careful, so its opposite is lazy.
questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to DILIGENT.

questions.explanation: For everyone in a hall to hear, the manager must have spoken loudly.
questions.q: Complete the sentence: The manager spoke so ___ that everyone in the hall could hear him.

questions.explanation: A blessing in disguise is something that seems bad at first but turns out to be beneficial.
questions.q: What does the idiom A BLESSING IN DISGUISE mean?

questions.explanation: The nearer subject officers is plural, so the plural verb were is required.
questions.q: Fill in the blank: Neither the clerk nor the officers ___ present yesterday.

questions.explanation: Benevolent means showing kindness and goodwill toward others.
questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to BENEVOLENT.

questions.explanation: The standard pattern is apologize to a person for an offence, so to is correct.
questions.q: Fill in the blank: She apologized ___ her friend for arriving late.
